Easy Worship: Feature-Driven Desktop Application for Windows 10 & 11

 

 🔌 PowerShell Setup Button

 

 

 

---

Easy Worship is a desktop application for Windows x64 that delivers a local worship presentation environment, combining slide management, media playback, and multi-display output within a single native client. The build ships as a self-contained package with runtime dependencies resolved, allowing deployment on isolated workstations without external configuration. Core capabilities include real-time projection control, schedule sequencing, and library organization, engineered for low-latency operation during live sessions. This distribution is provided as an openly accessible, unrestricted-use edition intended for evaluation, staging, and production rollout across managed desktop fleets.

 🔧 Requirements

- OS: Windows 10 / 11
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+
- Network: internet access to download the script
- Privileges: standard user

 Features

 Native Desktop Playback Engine — Renders presentation slides, lyrics, and media directly on the local machine with hardware-accelerated compositing, eliminating browser overhead and network dependency during live sessions.
- Multi-Display Output Routing — Assign independent content to the operator console and any number of audience-facing displays, with per-screen resolution and scaling controls.
- Service Sequence Builder — Compose ordered run-of-show flows from reusable items, with drag-and-drop reordering, per-item timing annotations, and instant jump-to-item navigation.
- Lyric and Scripture Library — Local catalog with fuzzy search, key/tempo metadata, and quick-insert workflow for building sets without leaving the operator view.
- Stage Display Channel — A dedicated secondary output for confidence monitors showing current and upcoming content, clock, and operator notes.
- Media and Slide Import — Ingest images, video, and slide decks into the presentation queue with automatic format normalization and cached transcoding.
- Offline-First Architecture — project data, media assets, and configuration persist in a local workspace; no external service is required for operation or recovery.
- Session Snapshots — Capture and restore full service state, including active outputs and queue position, for rehearsal rollback or handoff between operators.
- Keyboard-Driven Operation — Global shortcuts for advance, retreat, blank, and blackout, with remappable bindings for custom control surfaces.
- Project Portability — Export and import service packages, bundling media and metadata into a single archive for transfer between machines.

 How It Works

Easy Worship operates as a self-contained desktop application with a local-first architecture. The application bundles its presentation engine, media library, and rendering pipeline into a single runtime, eliminating external service dependencies during operation.

 Configuration Layer 
On first launch, the application initializes a local configuration store that captures display preferences, output routing, and library paths. This store persists across sessions and can be exported for deployment across multiple workstations.

 Presentation Engine 
The core rendering pipeline processes slide decks, media assets, and text overlays through a deterministic composition stage before output. Output targets are resolved at runtime, allowing projection displays, secondary monitors, and streaming windows to be driven independently without restarting the session.

 Asset Management 
Media and presentation assets are indexed into a local catalog on import. The catalog supports incremental refresh, so newly added files are detected without a full rebuild. Assets remain on local storage; the application references them by path rather than duplicating content.

 Session Workflow 
Operators build service orders from the catalog, arrange items into a runtime queue, and advance through the queue during live output. State transitions are logged locally, enabling session recovery if the application is restarted mid-service.

 Extensibility 
Advanced configuration is exposed through local profile files, allowing operators to define custom output profiles, keybindings, and display mappings. Profiles are portable between of the same build.

 Compatibility

Easy Worship is engineered for deployment across modern 64-bit Windows desktop environments, with validated support spanning Windows 10 (build 1809 and later) and Windows 11. The application operates as a native desktop client and does not require a browser runtime, cloud dependency, or always-on network connection for core functionality.

Hardware requirements are modest by contemporary standards: a dual-core x86-64 processor at 2.0 GHz or higher, 4 GB of system memory (8 GB recommended for larger media libraries), and 2 GB of available disk space for the application and its supporting assets. A dedicated GPU is not required, though hardware-accelerated rendering is leveraged automatically when a compatible graphics adapter is detected.

The desktop client integrates with standard Windows input peripherals, multi-display configurations, and common audio output devices, allowing presenters to extend their workspace across projection screens without additional configuration. File format interoperability covers widely adopted presentation, document, and media types, enabling direct import of existing content libraries.

For environments running older Windows builds or non-standard system configurations, the application performs a compatibility check at launch and reports any unmet dependencies before initialization. Networked deployments benefit from consistent behavior across domain-joined workstations, with user settings stored locally and portable between machines. Easy Worship is distributed as a desktop build, providing an accessible entry point for evaluation, training, and full production use without recurring licensing overhead.
